passes.summary: Kernel, module contract, reference module, memory system, CI and ADR baseline.
Master plan, parity matrix and roadmap approved; the rejected plan shapes recorded.
Postgres data spine, settings repository, Redis cooldowns, BullMQ worker, telemetry and /setup.
P1 audit: shared retry policy, setup permission proof and a worker Redis readiness ping.
Moderation cases, /mod, scanner, native AutoMod plan, appeals, security, quarantine and /verify.
P2 audit and case-store proofs; live Discord actions remain explicitly unproven.
Community suite: leveling, economy, reaction roles, welcome, starboard, tickets, giveaways and content.
AI provider, hard guild caps, exact-index RAG, deflection, explanations, summaries and classification.
Economy hardening: ledger-derived balances, guild lock, stable idempotency keys and explicit refusals.
Baseline commit, six research pages, memory v2 machine files, renderer and extended checks.
Channel resolver, all nine fetch sites migrated, obfuscation fixture and audit:channels.
Required/optional intents, INTENT_PROFILE, /setup capability report, audit:intents and P4.5 close.
Portability: export bundle, transactional restore, rollback, deletion receipts, level/transcript importers and drift report.
First live run: AI Team#5758 online, 10 commands registered, Qwen3:8b mention replies in #ai-chat; dev-only test seam and think:false adapter.
Dev-only prefix bridge and live command proof; bot-authored mention chat gated to DEV_GUILD_ID; /ticket stats ordering fixed; clear-then-register command sync with read-back.
Public release packaging: Keystone repo, README/AGENTS, AGPL-3.0 licence, safe drift-only command sync and explicit resync.
P6 dashboard/API foundation: OAuth2/PKCE sessions, BigInt guild authz with bot membership, read-only HTML/API reads, Postgres stores and no-paid-service rule.
P6 settings writes: CSRF-protected dashboard form and PATCH API through SettingsService, module Zod validation, cross-guild/non-admin/bot-absent tests.
Invite tracking: cached-counter attribution, durable invite_joins, /invites leaderboard|stats|who and advisory flags; live 11-command registration and dev-bridge run.
Cold-cache invite attribution records no inviter; unused refresh-token storage removed; command-sync and MEE6 claims corrected.
Invite gateway boundary: a gateway-independent tracker owns cache, queue and decisions; discord.js wiring is a translation layer with a direct serialization test.
Dashboard server boundaries: ordered route table, per-area handlers, one session context, shared render/http modules and one settings-write CSRF gate.
Link/phishing filter: local host blocklist and punycode detection in the security engine, /mod links review queue, and a dev marker seam for MCP-driven live proof.
Profanity/zalgo filter: operator-owned banned words on Unicode word edges, a combining-mark threshold, /mod filters review action, and the live delete-mode link proof.

Auto-responder: exact/contains/regex triggers in the community record seam, one reply with deterministic precedence, per-trigger cooldowns and /tools admin actions; live gateway proof plus a live profanity delete-mode proof.

Command tree: every existing hub now registers real Discord subcommands (12 roots, 77 subcommands), `/help` reads the live registry, the catalog is generated, and boot sync plus commands:doctor compare the full option shape instead of names alone.

Environment check plus synthetic slash harness: real nested /mod ban through asInteractionLike and dispatch, exact local Postgres/Redis blocker errors, Ollama warm retry, and a duplicate-process fix verified by one-reply MCP transcript.

Audit logging: the seventh module adds /logging setup|channel|events|status|retention|export|disable, five event kinds written to an append-only ledger before best-effort Discord delivery, a case observer, SQL + in-memory stores and retention pruning. Live-proven for message edit/delete and moderation cases; member joins/leaves remain adapter-only.

Guild analytics: the eighth module adds /analytics overview|members|messages|commands|tickets|export as a read-only aggregate over logging_events, cases, invite_joins, tickets and a new append-only command_usage ledger. Every printed number names its source table; SQL and in-memory adapters share one port. Live bridge proof matched 2 stored audit events to 2 logged events and one MCP edit/delete to exactly 1 edited/1 deleted; Discord reports 14 roots / 90 subcommands.

In-bot configuration: `/config list | get | set | export` in the setup module reads and writes every registered module's per-guild settings through SettingsService and the owning Zod schema. One root, four subcommands, no second settings store. Live bridge proof set moderation.automod.links alert -> delete -> alert and rejected bogus without a write; Discord reports 15 roots / 94 subcommands.

In-Discord portability: `/export guild | user | import | delete | drift | rollback` in the setup module. Guild and user exports are real JSON file attachments; import defaults to a dry run and reads a Discord attachment through a size-capped reader; drift compares stored ids with the live gateway cache. One kernel ExportPort has a SQL adapter over the existing PortabilityService and a memory adapter that reads the live stores. Live bridge proof: a 12.8 KB guild bundle parsed with 49 settings / 1 case / 1 case event / 1 ledger row / 1 record and the printed checksum; a 2 KB member bundle; drift 1 missing -> 0 missing after restoring the channel; wrong-id delete and memory rollback refused. Discord reports 16 roots / 100 subcommands.

Music, the last named v1.0 root: `/music play | queue | add | remove | clear | skip | stop | status`. The saved queue is real and persists in `community_records` (kind `music_queue`, key `default`); the SQL adapter locks the guild row so concurrent adds cannot exceed the cap, and the in-memory adapter serializes mutations per guild. Playback is not installed: no voice or Lavalink client and no LAVALINK_URL exist in this build, so play, skip and stop refuse with that exact reason and status prints `playback UNAVAILABLE`. Live bridge proof in #ai-chat: status disabled, `/config set music.enabled=true`, two adds, queue 2/25, play refusal, remove to 1/25, skip refusal, disable, and an add refused while disabled. Discord reports 17 roots / 108 subcommands.

Context menus, the last unbuilt v1.0 surface: four right-click commands (Report message, Case history, Rank card, Explain with AI) now cross the same adapter, registry, guards, cooldowns and dispatcher as slash commands. The kernel models command type, validates menu names separately, keys the registry and drift check by type, and audits the separate 15 + 15 context-menu budgets. Report message opens a real case with the message id and a capped excerpt; Case history reads the same case rows as /mod history behind ModerateMembers; Rank card reads the same XP projection as /rank view; Explain with AI calls AiService.explain and honours the explanations switch. A single memory-mode boot found all four menus missing, cleared once and registered 21 application commands; Discord now reports 17 roots / 108 subcommands / 2 user menus / 2 message menus with no drift. The MCP cannot right-click, so invocation is not claimed live and each path is covered by adapter and command tests.

Subcommand gap audit and the `/setup` hub. The repository's only saved per-root plan names 12 roots / 59 subcommands, not 18 / 160; the 18th root is unnamed and 47 subcommands remain unaccounted for, so the 160 target is recorded as unverified rather than invented. The largest honest gap was `/setup` (5 planned, 0 registered): it now ships status, module, verify, import-preview and reset. Status is the previous readiness report; module lists/inspects/toggles a module through ConfigPort and its Zod schema; verify checks database, settings parsing and the catalog read-only; import previews an attachment through the existing ExportPort with dryRun true and points at `/export import`; reset exposes the existing repository clear through ConfigPort.reset and leaves cases/XP/ledger untouched. No new root, store or migration. Live bridge: 9 modules / 2 disabled, music enabled then reset, read-back showed the schema default disabled; doctor reports 17 roots / 113 subcommands, 0 errors. MCP cannot attach a file, so import is test-covered. 365 tests / 56 files.

Appeal hub: /appeal open | status replaces the option-only root. open appends the existing target-only appealed event; status reads case_events through the new CaseStore.listEvents, so a review that changes the case state cannot erase the appeal. The root keeps one global slot, adds two real subcommands, no table and no new dependency. Live bridge: warning case #1 opened against the MCP author, appeal opened, status #1 · warn · appealed · 1 appeal; after !mod review case=1 status still read #1 · warn · reviewed · 1 appeal; a case against the bot was refused as Case #2 is not one of your cases. Discord reports 17 roots / 115 subcommands / 4 context menus. Tests 368 / 56 files.

Verify hub, the saved plan's last two names: `/verify start | status` replaces the optionless root. `start` parses the join-gate settings, refuses an already-verified member, refuses a record that is not quarantined, and sends the existing verification button by DM; a DM failure is an explicit refusal that names the cause. `status` reads a new `MemberStore` over the existing `members` table (`guild_id`, `user_id`, `joined_at`, `quarantined`, `verified_at`) instead of gateway roles. The shared `completeVerification` path performs the quarantine action first and writes `verified_at` only after it succeeds; the in-guild legacy button and the DM button use the same path. One in-memory store, one Drizzle store, no migration. Live memory mode: `!verify status` read no record, `!verify start` refused with the exact DM error, a second status still read no record; `commands:doctor` reports 17 roots / 117 subcommands / 4 menus with no drift. The MCP bot cannot receive the DM or click the button, so completion is test-covered and not claimed live. Tests 371 / 57 files; .env DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL still ECONNREFUSED.

Join-gate state machine repair. An enforced join-gate hold now writes a quarantined `members` row through `SecurityCoordinator`; the write happens only after `actions.quarantine` succeeds, only for `join-gate.*` findings, and anti-raid/anti-nuke holds do not create a verify row or button. `MemberStore.markQuarantined` was added to the kernel port, the in-memory store and the Drizzle store; it clears any previous `verified_at`, preserves `joined_at`, and needs no migration. `/verify start` now refuses a member with no record and a record that is not quarantined, status reports no record without suggesting a dead-end start, and `completeVerification` refuses no record/non-quarantined/verified/disabled-gate and transitions only a quarantined row after the action succeeds. Tests: join path, four-case command behavior, six completion transitions and the SQL quarantine upsert. Live memory mode: `!verify status` read no record and `!verify start` returned `No quarantine is recorded for you in this server. If you are restricted, ask a moderator.`; the join path and button click are not live because the MCP account is a bot. Tests 385 / 58 files; .env DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL still ECONNREFUSED.

Button wiring extraction. The appeal and verify rules moved out of `apps/bot/src/index.ts` (348 to 287 lines) into `apps/bot/src/moderation-buttons.ts`: `parseModerationButtonId` returns an appeal case id, a current guild-scoped verify route, or a legacy one-part verify route with the interaction guild; empty, foreign and over-segmented ids are ignored. `handleAppealButton` keeps the exact settings read, target-only case service call and replies; `handleVerifyButton` keeps the encoded-user identity check, DM/guild ephemeral rule and `completeVerification` call. No command, menu, reply string, registration or ledger count changed. `toReplyOptions` is exported from the adapter so button replies use the same conversion. 13 focused tests cover parsing, valid and refused appeal/verify paths, the DM reply route, malformed ids and the wrong-actor/gate-disabled refusals. The DM port move remains the only deferred audit finding. Tests 398 / 59 files; budget unchanged 17/100 roots · 117 subcommands · 4 context menus.

Join-gate DM ownership. `/verify start` no longer calls `ctx.community.actions.sendDM`; moderation now delivers its own direct message through `ModerationActions.directMessage`, a narrow member on the existing moderation port, with `ModerationDirectMessage` carrying content and components. The Discord moderation adapter fetches the user and maps a closed DM to `{ ok: false, detail }`; the command preserves the DM body, verify button, success reply, ephemeral rule and refusal text. The moderation tests record direct messages on the moderation port and build the context without any community port, proving the dependency is gone. No new port, file, table, migration, command or dependency. Tests 398 / 59 files; ledger unchanged 17/100 roots · 117 subcommands · 4 context menus. Live memory mode proved the no-record refusal and that no row was written; the MCP bot cannot receive a DM, so the send-success path is test-covered only. Both deferred audit findings are now cleared.

Forms, the first new root after the saved plan was completed: `/form create | edit | delete | list | panel | submit | review | export` is the tenth module. Two tables in migration 0011 — `forms` with a unique `(guild_id, key)` and `form_submissions` with a partial unique index on `(form_id, user_id) WHERE state = 'submitted'` — are justified by the review transition and the one-pending-application invariant. One `FormStore` has in-memory and Drizzle adapters; `FormService` owns field/answer validation, the draft/open/closed gates, the form and submission caps, the delete-only-without-history rule and the conditional `submitted → accepted/denied` transition. `panel` refuses a non-open form, posts in the invoking channel and records it; `delete` requires the key and refuses once a submission exists; `export` attaches `keystone.forms` JSON with a SHA-256 checksum. Modal input is deferred and named: `submit` takes the validated `answers` option, not a dead button. Live memory mode (exactly one process; no other bot was running): create → open → panel → submit `31778bdb…` → 1 pending → accepted with a note → 0 pending → export 1540 bytes / checksum `d1fd6d91…`; the downloaded file parsed as 1 form / 1 submission with the same panel channel, answers, state, reviewer and a checksum that recomputes. `commands:doctor` reports 18 roots / 125 subcommands / 2 user + 2 message menus with no drift. Tests 413 / 61 files; .env DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL still ECONNREFUSED.

Events, the first of the two plan roots the inventory found unbuilt: `/event create | edit | delete | list | rsvp | remind | export` is the eleventh module. Migration 0012 adds `events` and `event_rsvps`; a table is justified because an RSVP is relational state with one row per member and a capacity check that must be atomic, which a settings blob cannot enforce. One `EventStore` has in-memory and Drizzle adapters; the SQL adapter locks the event row and counts `going` rows inside the transaction. `EventService` owns the draft/open/closed lifecycle, date parsing, the event cap, the capacity bound, the delete-only-without-attendance rule and reminder bookkeeping; `rsvp` takes the member id from the interaction and has no user option, so no command can write another member's row. PGlite tests cover the unique `(event_id, user_id)` row, capacity, a decline freeing a seat, reminder counts and cascade delete. Live memory mode (exactly one process): create draft → open → rsvp going 1/2 → remind (reminder 1, 1 going) → rsvp not going 0/2 → rsvp going 1/2 → export 1242 bytes / checksum `95023b52…`; the downloaded file carried the same event, capacity, reminder count, reviewer id and a checksum that recomputes; delete was refused while the RSVP exists. `commands:doctor` reports 19 roots / 132 subcommands / 2 user + 2 message menus with no drift. Also removed dead `allSubmissions` from the forms store and recorded the plan's per-root table in Master-Plan (72 planned names across 13 built roots plus /modmail; 132 registered). Tests 425 / 63 files; .env DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL still ECONNREFUSED.

Modmail, the last plan root: `/modmail setup | open | reply | close | transcript | stats` is the twelfth module. Migration 0013 adds `modmail_threads` and `modmail_messages`; tables are justified because the product is an ownership rule, one active thread per member (partial unique index), an append-only conversation and a transcript archived exactly once. One `ModmailStore` port has in-memory and Drizzle adapters; `ModmailService` owns the privacy check, the open → claimed → closed lifecycle, the first-staff-reply claim, unread counters per side, message/subject caps and the SHA-256 transcript. A caller who is neither owner nor staff gets the same `was not found` refusal as a missing thread, so the command cannot confirm someone else's mail. Closing is a single conditional update that stores the transcript, checksum and message count; a duplicate close refuses and writes nothing. `stats` lists up to ten active thread ids so staff can discover a thread to answer instead of counting only. Tests: 6 module tests cover the positive flow, owner/staff visibility, foreign and missing threads, closed-thread reply, duplicate close, one-active-thread, setup write, disabled drain and caps; 4 PGlite tests read the raw tables for the active-owner index, claim counters, single archive and guild-scoped stats. Live memory mode (exactly one process): setup enabled, open `0f7dbc9c…`, member reply 2 messages, live transcript, close with 2 messages archived and checksum `c3c539706ed70e53…`, duplicate close refused, archived transcript read back, stats 1/0/2, disabled open refused and setup restored. `commands:doctor` reports 20 roots / 138 subcommands / 2 user + 2 message menus with no drift. The Master-Plan now records all six modmail names: 72 planned names across 14 built roots, 66 registered names beyond those (38 extra names inside plan roots, 28 in six roots the plan never named), and the handoff's 160 still has 88 unrecorded names and still does not name its 18 roots; the bot's 138 are 22 short of the raw count. Tests 435 / 65 files; .env DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL still ECONNREFUSED.

Truth pass: memory and docs audited against the code. `pnpm audit:claims` is now part of `pnpm check`; it computes the registry (20 roots / 138 subcommands / 158 actions / 4 context menus / 12 modules), reads the vitest JSON report so the test/file counts are measured rather than typed, compares the current-tense counts in AGENTS.md and README.md, checks `project.metrics`, proves the `/help changelog` pointer matches the latest pass, and rejects a shipped Components V2 claim while no `packages/ui` or `IsComponentsV2` code exists. `memory:check` now checks that AGENTS.md lists every module directory, that its `Current state` date matches `project.updatedAt`, that Status `Now` names the latest pass, that every written Curriculum lesson is linked, and that local Markdown links resolve. The stale claims are corrected: AGENTS.md said twelve roots and omitted forms/events/modmail; `/help changelog` still reported pass 26; the parity matrix, features.json and three research pages claimed V2 work that does not exist; Status.md called the pass-40 ledger current and said Docker was absent even though Docker Desktop 29.9.2 is running with no compose services started; AI and community status pages still claimed a 10/100 ledger; events claimed 151 actions. No product behaviour changed except the changelog text. Tests 436 / 65 files; compose Postgres/Redis are still not started, so the live window remains memory mode until pass 44.

Live substrate, not a feature pass. `docker compose up -d --wait postgres redis` started Postgres 16.15 and Redis; `pnpm db:migrate` applied all 13 migrations. The first live run exposed a real defect: `migrate()` sent raw `BEGIN` through postgres.js, which rejects pooled transaction control with `UNSAFE_TRANSACTION`. `SqlRunner` now requires a driver `transaction` primitive; the Postgres runner uses `client.begin`, the PGlite runner wraps BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, and two PGlite regressions prove a failed migration leaves neither its table nor its ledger row and a successful one commits both. New `pnpm probe:live` (not in `pnpm check`, which must pass without a database) exercised nine paths and wrote `memory/machine/live.json`: 13 migrations, a settings row surviving a pool close/reopen, a Redis cooldown shared by two clients, two BullMQ enqueues producing one handler call and a completed Postgres receipt, portability dry-run/import-checksum/rollback/deletion-receipt, and `/healthz` returning `database: postgres`. Five rows flipped to live-verified with `liveEvidence` check ids (`portability.restore-and-config-hash`, `portability.dry-run-import-diff`, `portability.rollback-window`, `portability.deletion-receipt`, `security.backup-restore`); `operations.in-bot-config` now also cites the restart check. `memory:check` validates `live.json` and every `liveEvidence` reference; `memory:render` generates `06-Operations/Live-Window.md`; `audit:claims` checks the documented Docker version and live-service claims against the report. Still not live: human slash/right-click, Discord OAuth, a persistent production worker, gateway member events, music playback and analytics reads over Postgres. Tests 438 / 66 files.

Feature pass: temporary moderation expiry and scheduled/reminder delivery now share one delayed BullMQ queue consumed in the bot process, because the worker has no Discord client and adding a second Discord adapter would be worse. Cases gained `expires_at` (migration 0014) and `claimExpiry`, so two workers cannot release the same ban/role twice; a failed release restores the timestamp, and startup recovery expires overdue cases and reschedules future ones. `/mod ban` accepts a duration and `/mod temp-role` is a real subcommand; both write the case before the Discord action. `/tools reminder|schedule` now enqueue `content.deliver` with a record id; delivery claims the record with one conditional update so the timer and the 60-second sweep cannot both send, restores the claim on failure, and marks `sent` only after Discord accepts. Tests are 457 in 68 files; the live probe is 12/12, adding a delayed timer, a real Postgres case expiry and real reminder/scheduled delivery. Temp-ban/temp-role moved from open to shipped-in-repo; all three timer rows stay liveVerified false because the Discord port was recorded, not sent to a guild.

Lifecycle pass: panic mode and goodbye messages, with no new scheduler. `/mod panic state:status|on|off` asks the adapter which text channels it changed, snapshots each existing @everyone SendMessages overwrite before denying it, persists one community_records row before replying, and restores only those channels; failed restores stay in the row so a second off retries them, and a channel already denied is never unlocked. It requires Administrator and has no timer. `/tools goodbye` writes goodbye.* in the existing community settings; WelcomeService.handleLeave sends the configured text with {user}/{server} and deliberately has no role or DM branch. Tests are 471 in 71 files; the live probe is 13/13 and adds a panic-snapshot Postgres round-trip. panic-mode and welcome-goodbye moved from open to shipped-in-repo; both stay liveVerified false because the Discord overwrite calls and GuildMemberRemove were adapter-tested, not observed on a gateway.

Teaching pass: all 14 lessons are written and now machine-checked. memory/machine/lessons.json records each lesson's path, source files, proof commands and taught counts; memory:check verifies the paths and package scripts exist, the five required sections and Curriculum link are present, and every count matches commands.json, live.json or project.json. The README Docker quickstart now matches apps/web/src/runtime.ts: gateway-only hosts run bot + worker, while the default stack needs SESSION_SECRET before the optional web service boots. Lesson 7's doubled heading was fixed. No product behaviour, feature row or test count changed; the live probe remains 13/13.

Truth gate: memory/machine/claims.json names the documents that speak in the present tense, and memory:check now recomputes roots, subcommands, actions, context menus, modules, tests and passes from the machine files. A current-tense contradiction fails unless the sentence names the pass it describes; a capability claim with no code evidence (Components V2, i18n, the Next.js shell) must be marked planned; a governed page cannot call the live services stopped. The drift named by the completion plan is corrected across README, Status, the module Spec/Status ledger blocks and the stale Docker/expiry notes, and the root CONTRIBUTING/GOVERNANCE/SECURITY/CODE_OF_CONDUCT files plus issue/PR templates were added. No product behaviour changed; tests remain 471 in 71 files and the live probe remains 13/13.

P6 schema-driven settings widgets: the dashboard settings page is generated from each module's Zod schema (booleans, bounded numbers, enums, text/textarea, one-per-line arrays, validated JSON fallback), and named form fields parse back into the patch SettingsService validates. A new kernel AuditStore port, in-memory adapter and Drizzle audit_events adapter record every accepted update/reset with actor, source and dotted-path diff; /config and /setup pass the command actor, and the settings page shows the newest rows. The carrier remains the framework-free apps/web HTML app; no Next.js shell, packages/ui or second settings schema was added. Two defects fixed: the secret-key filter hid maxOutputTokens, and explicit undefined optional values could become NULL. Live probe is 14/14; the new web-schema-widgets check drove real local HTTP login/session/CSRF and the schema form on Postgres (save 9, audit row, 5000 rejected at 400 with no second row); OAuth exchange used a fake port, so live Discord OAuth remains open. Tests 488 / 73 files.

P6 fleet view and config templates: /dashboard/fleet lists the guilds the signed-in user can manage with their enabled modules, and three built-in templates (alert-first moderation, strict moderation, quiet optional modules) can be previewed against a multi-guild selection. The preview deep-merges each template patch over the current settings, parses the result with the module's own Zod schema, and diffs it with the audit helper; nothing is written. Apply is bound to a SHA-256 fingerprint of the displayed plan, refuses a stale or missing preview at 409/400, and re-authorizes every selected guild (permission + bot membership) before calling SettingsService.update. Each accepted module write appends one dashboard audit row. The carrier remains the framework-free apps/web HTML app; no Next.js shell, second settings schema or template table was added. Tests 502 / 74 files; live probe 15/15, adding web-fleet-templates: two guilds on Postgres, preview diff, wrong-fingerprint refusal, one moderation write and one dashboard audit row per guild; OAuth exchange used a fake port, so live Discord OAuth remains open.

P6 config export, import and drift: a guild's effective module settings download as a checksummed JSON bundle (credential-shaped keys omitted), and import parses and schema-validates the file before previewing the exact per-setting diff. Apply is bound to a SHA-256 fingerprint of the displayed plan, refuses an edited checksum at 400 and a stale preview at 409, reuses SettingsService.update (one dashboard audit row per module) and stores the applied bundle as the guild's baseline. A new config_baselines table (migration 0015) and ConfigBaselineStore port power a drift page that compares baseline to live and reports unreadable or absent baselines honestly. The carrier is still the framework-free apps/web app; no Next.js shell, template table or second settings schema was added. Tests 515 / 76 files; live probe 16/16, adding web-config-export-import-drift over real local HTTP and Postgres: multipart upload, preview with no write, 400/409 refusals, one audited AI write, stored baseline, no drift, then one drift after an out-of-band change; OAuth exchange used a fake port.

P6 saved templates: an admin saves a guild's effective settings as a named snapshot, lists, renames/refreshes, deletes and applies it to selected guilds through the same plan → SHA-256 preview fingerprint → re-authorization → per-module SettingsService.update → dashboard audit row path as the built-ins. Every snapshot is parsed by each module's own Zod schema on save; a stored row that drifts out of validity is reported and refused at 400, never applied. Create, update and delete append their own audit rows. One kernel port with in-memory and Drizzle adapters, migration 0016 and no template marketplace or second write path. The carrier is still the framework-free apps/web app. Tests 526 / 79 files; live probe 17/17, adding web-saved-templates over real local HTTP and Postgres: save, list, two-guild preview with no write, tampered and stale 409 refusals, one audited write per guild, an invalidated row refused at 400, and audited create/update/delete; OAuth exchange used a fake port.

P6 dashboard analytics: the dashboard page and GET /api/v1/guilds/:id/analytics reuse the existing AnalyticsStore over logging_events, cases, invite_joins, tickets and command_usage. There is no analytics table, new writer or second aggregation path. One bounded 1-90 day window; the page prints every source table row count, distinguishes current-state ticket/case values, and says plainly when a window has no retained rows instead of implying no Discord activity. Migration 0017 adds only the missing window indexes for cases, invite joins and tickets. Tests 533 / 80 files; live probe 18/18, adding web-analytics-aggregates over real local HTTP and Postgres: seven seeded audit rows, three cases, two invite joins, three tickets and three command runs matched every API/page aggregate, an empty guild was named, days=91/abc were refused at 400 and signed-out reads at 401; OAuth exchange used a fake port.

P6 scoped API tokens: one `ApiTokenStore` port (in-memory + Drizzle, migration 0018) behind a `keystone_…` secret that is shown once and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. A token is bound to one guild and a subset of guild:read, analytics:read and settings:write; `authorizeApiGuild` lets it feed the existing `/api/v1` handlers while checking guild, scope and bot membership, and a session still needs CSRF while a token does not. Issue and revoke use the guild write gate and append one dashboard audit row each. A per-token fixed window (60/min) buckets by token id or address; `/api/v1/openapi.json` is generated from an operation table that a test walks against the route registry in both directions. Tests 553 / 82 files; live probe 20/20, adding web-api-tokens over real local HTTP and Postgres: the secret never reached a column, the token read the existing handlers, foreign-guild and wrong-scope calls were 403, anonymous/bogus bearers 401, the per-token window returned 429 + Retry-After then recovered, revoke returned 401 and audited exactly once.

P6 session hardening: the opaque Postgres session cookie is re-keyed every 15 minutes on a safe GET, so the previous cookie is dead immediately; logout asks the OAuth port to revoke the Discord access token before deleting the row (best effort, the local session always dies); fixed-window limits cover the auth, dashboard, write and API route classes with 429 + Retry-After and recovery in the next window; and WEB_OWNER_IDS gates an instance console plus a sign-out-every-user action that a guild admin cannot reach. Six new HTTP tests and one PGlite test cover rotation, replay, revocation ordering and failure, per-class limits, anonymous limits and the owner gate. Tests 540 / 80 files; live probe 19/19, adding web-session-hardening over real local HTTP and Postgres: 401 anonymous / 403 guild admin / 200 owner, the owner's revocation killed the admin cookie, all four classes returned 429 with Retry-After then recovered, /healthz stayed exempt, the rotated cookie replaced the old one, and logout revoked through the fake OAuth port. Token revocation is asserted at the port; no live Discord revocation or login is claimed.

P6 webhooks and Idempotency-Key: the second half of the public-API block. One `WebhookStore` port (in-memory + Drizzle, migration 0019) over `webhook_subscriptions` and `webhook_deliveries`; a `whsec_…` signing secret is shown once and sealed with the same `SecretBox` as Discord tokens. Creating, test-pinging and removing an endpoint use the session -> guild authorization -> CSRF gate and append `webhook.create` / `webhook.test` / `webhook.delete` dashboard audit rows. Delivery is an outbox row written before the network call, signed `t=<unix>,v1=HMAC-SHA256(<t>.<body>)`; one drainer in the web process attempts due rows, retries a failure three times with exponential backoff, then leaves a terminal failed receipt with the last HTTP status. Settings updates, token issue and token revoke enqueue events. `Idempotency-Key` on a token settings write reuses the existing `PostgresIdempotencyStore`/`job_receipts`: the same key and body replay the stored status and exact response bytes (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`), a different body is 409 `idempotency_conflict`, and only the first call writes settings or audit. `response_body` is text rather than jsonb so a replay is byte-identical. Tests 569 / 85 files; live probe 22/22, adding web-webhooks (a local receiver verified the HMAC independently, an always-500 receiver was tried three times then failed and the receipt page showed 500, non-loopback http was refused at 400, and both removals were audited) and web-idempotency-key (replay, 409 conflict, one audit row and the stored fingerprint) over real local HTTP and Postgres.

P6 session lifecycle, the last landable piece of the phase. The opaque session gains `last_seen_at`, a sealed refresh token and an access expiry. A session unused past the configurable idle window (default 30 minutes, `WEB_SESSION_IDLE_MS`, minimum 1 minute) is refused and its row deleted, while activity inside the window moves the idle clock without extending the absolute 7-day lifetime. An expired Discord access token is refreshed through the OAuth port, the rotated refresh token is sealed and persisted in the same write, and one in-flight refresh per session means two concurrent requests spend one token. A refused token (invalid_grant) deletes the session; a transport failure keeps it for a later attempt. Logout now revokes the sealed refresh grant instead of only the access token. Migration 0020 adds `refresh_token`, `access_expires_at` and `last_seen_at`; existing sessions get one idle window and an access expiry from their absolute expiry. The instance page shows the idle window. Three HTTP tests and one PGlite test cover stale-session deletion, activity touching, single-flight refresh with rotation, and a replayed spent token. Tests 573 / 85 files; live probe 23/23, adding web-session-idle-refresh over real local HTTP and Postgres: idle inside/outside the window with row deletion, two concurrent requests made exactly one refresh call, the rotated sealed token was stored, and restoring the spent token returned 401 and deleted the session. The probe's OAuth exchange, refresh and revocation are fake; live Discord OAuth is still unclaimed.

P7 Components V2 layer, signed component routing and form modals. `packages/ui` now exists as a framework-free package: `layout()` builds a typed container/text/section/action-row tree and enforces Discord's 40-component and 4,000-character budgets plus row and option shapes, and `modal()` builds Label-wrapped text inputs under a five-row, 45-character-title limit; both throw instead of truncating. The kernel owns `V2Component`/`ModalSpec` and adds `createComponentSigner` (HMAC-signed `k1:` ids carrying namespace, action, payload and expiry, at most 100 chars) and `ComponentRouter` (kind + namespace + action match, signature and expiry check, guild and permission gates, UserError to ephemeral reply). `apps/bot/src/adapt.ts` maps the tree to discord.js builders and sets `MessageFlags.IsComponentsV2`; one component listener now handles buttons, selects and modal submits, handing legacy moderation ids to their existing handler. `/form panel` is a V2 container with signed Apply and staff buttons; Apply opens a modal built from the form's fields and a valid submit calls the same FormService.submit, while a missing answer is refused by name and a form over five questions keeps the command path. `INTERACTION_SECRET` is optional: without it the key is per-process so pre-restart panels are honestly stale. No i18n work and no other panel was migrated. Tests 604 / 89 files; live probe 24/24, adding web-component-panels through the real discord.js adapter and router on Postgres: panel JSON, modal title and inputs, one stored submission, a bad submit refused with no row, an expired id refused before the handler, a member refused and a manager shown the pending queue. A live gateway click and modal submit are not claimed.
